patterns.prevention:
• Audit all coaches currently assigned to childcare centres and remove those with documented engagement or energy concerns before they cause additional cancellations.

• Establish a backup coach protocol so centres always have a replacement within 48 hours if their primary coach becomes unavailable or needs to be removed.

• Brief coaches assigned to centres on expectations for consistency, attendance, and engagement level—make clear that centres expect the same energy every session.

• Schedule manager check-ins at each centre within two weeks to gather direct feedback on coach performance and address any emerging issues before they escalate to cancellation.

patterns.prevention:
• Schedule quarterly business reviews with centre directors to understand budget cycles and competitive positioning before renewal periods.

• Develop a tiered pricing model offering that allows centres to reduce session frequency or scale back without switching providers entirely.

• Create a monthly touchpoint call with each centre manager to gather real-time feedback on program value and identify satisfaction issues before cancellation notices arrive.

• Build case studies showing cost-per-child and developmental outcomes to help centres justify our programs to families and educators when competing against in-house alternatives.
